# Casefile v0.10.0

## Independent investigation access

- Fixed MCP startup and catalogue discovery requiring access to unrelated investigations. Discovery
  now reads configuration and the project registry without recursively inventorying Store contents.
- Scoped reads, diagnostics, and mutations read only the selected investigation and its actual
  referenced dependencies. Unreadable unrelated files and nested investigations no longer block
  ordinary MCP work; permission failures in the selected scope or a required dependency still name
  the affected path and fail.
- Configuring a disposable SQLite cache no longer starts whole-Store observation at Provider startup
  or after an ordinary scoped apply. Full-index reads and refreshes remain explicit operations.
- Preserved stale-preview rejection, external-edit protection, containment, and deletion approval.

## Upgrade notes

Provider protocol is now **6**. Upgrade the executable, plugin, and API clients together, then start
a new host session. Catalogue freshness covers configuration and registry data; scoped freshness and
diagnostic coverage describe the selected investigation and explicit dependencies. Whole-Store
duplicate-ID and incoming-reference checks require an explicit whole-Store check.

Bare ticket and epic references resolve within their investigation. Bare decision references also
check the project's decision log and still report ambiguity. Cross-investigation references require
an explicit canonical Store-relative path within the same project; unresolved legacy bare references
produce actionable diagnostics instead of searching unrelated investigations.

The planning format remains **1**. Existing activated Stores and progress logs need no conversion or
reactivation. This release does not rewrite live references or broaden filesystem permissions.

Matched Codex and Claude packages include native executables for Linux, macOS, and Windows on x86-64
and ARM64. No measured speedup percentage is claimed for this correction.
